questions.text_english:
(1) Five enterprises received approval and grants for prototype development of sustainable educational toys.

(2) The government authorities, educational institutions and EdTech start-ups are planning to introduce state-of-the-art, made-in-India educational toys that not only throw light on Indian values and civilisations, but also help in developing children's critical thinking, and decision-making skills.

(3) One such enterprise is working on different types of projects that can teach children how electromagnets and magnetic fields work. These projects can resolve a lot of issues in many schools in tier two and three cities that don't have proper infrastructure. Another is working on an excavation site to teach children about ancient Indian civilizations. It has implanted a few artifacts at the site, which the children will have to find so that they are able to learn how to preserve and label artifacts. Another start up has proposed to create miniaturized labs for schools in tier 2 and 3 cities where children can learn concepts of Physics. We will ensure that these prototypes are developed within a year and then the production can be scaled up,says the senior manager of the project talking about the importance of indigenously-built educational toys.

(4) Playtime is vital for the cognitive development of children and toys are an essential component that helps enhance specific cognitive abilities and skill sets. Well-designed toys ignite students' curiosity, increase focus and can be very beneficial in helping them master a skill and enhance understanding. These can be in the form of visuals, auditory aids, kinesthetic, or a mixture of all three.says HOD, Early Childhood Education.

(5) Toys offer an engaging avenue to teach mathematical, verbal, problem-solving skills. Toys that engage students in experiential learning enhance their special awareness and fine motor skills. Those designed for two or more players help students develop better social skills as they learn to negotiate, settle differences, etc, with their peers.

(6) Experiential gadgets and toys enable students to learn faster and retain lessons longer. A child's interest is piqued when he is taught in a contextual framework as opposed to rote learning. The Indian education system has been witnessing several innovations with the development of toys and gadgets that can be used and felt in person or through VR platforms across subjects, be it Science, Technology, Math or Engineering.

questions.text_english:
(1) People below the age of 20 and above the age of 50 are more likely to believe fake news. Those relatively new to the use of the internet still do not grasp the concept of fake information over these platforms, reveals a new survey 'Countering Misinformation in India.' This survey has been conducted jointly by Internet and Mobile Association of India (IAMAI).

(2) At least 40% of the respondents believed in 'misinformation' received over social media if it came with leading backgrounds and evidence, while 34% of them believe the information when it is shared by a trustworthy organization.

(3) The dominant factor that drives people to forward such information is their belief that it might benefit others and help in their safety. In fact, that was the response of almost 50% of the respondents. This was compounded by the fact that at least 20% of the respondents expressed their lack of trust in conventional media thus their faith in contents shared by common people over social media.

(4) But even then, newspapers still remain the top source of information for most. At least 53% of the respondents trust what is generally perceived as neutral media and only 29% trust technology and social media platforms.

(5) However, what was surprising was that almost 45% of the respondents did not even know about the existence of fact-checking organization and most did not even know that journalists had to verify data before they let it out. Only 26% of the respondents believe that it is the responsibility of the media to curb or identify fake news. Many respondents also put the responsibility of identifying such fake news on an individual.

(6) The survey has found that first time or early users of the Internet platforms are more susceptible to fake news than others. There is a need for building capacities and creating a National Civic Digital Literacy Strategic Plan.

key_points: The passage uses them interchangeably to refer to inaccurate information.

sub_questions.solution: Based on the text, both terms are used interchangeably to describe false or inaccurate content shared on platforms, though 'misinformation' often implies data perceived to be credible due to 'evidence' or 'trustworthy' sources.

sub_questions.solution: The survey identifies two specific age groups susceptible to believing fake news: individuals below the age of 20 and those above 50. Additionally, first-time or early users of internet platforms are significantly more vulnerable to misinformation than experienced users.

sub_questions.solution: There is no consensus on who should police fake news; only 26% of respondents believe it is the media's duty to identify it. (b) Your school recently organized Y-20 Chaupal under G-20 initiative. The theme chosen for the event was Health and Wellness. sub_questions.text_english: Article writing
sub_questions.solution:
TELEVISION: A DYNAMIC LEARNING TOOL
By Geeta

Television, often dismissed as a source of mindless entertainment, holds immense potential as a powerful educational tool. With easy access in most homes, T.V. provides an inexpensive platform for lifelong learning. Specialized channels offer a wealth of informative content, ranging from daily news updates to insightful panel discussions. Documentaries focusing on science, history, and astronomy—such as those on National Geographic—can bring theoretical concepts to life, making complex topics easier to grasp. Moreover, television serves as a window to the world, offering glimpses into foreign cultures, global architecture, diverse food habits, and art forms, which broadens a student's worldview. If curated thoughtfully, television can effectively complement formal classroom instruction. It is time we recognize its value not just as a medium of leisure, but as a gateway to knowledge that is accessible and engaging for all students.

sub_questions.text_english: Report writing
sub_questions.solution:
Y-20 CHAUPAL: A DIALOGUE ON HEALTH AND WELLNESS
By Neeraj, Student Editor

On June 5, 2026, our school organized a Y-20 Chaupal under the G-20 initiative, focusing on the theme of 'Health and Wellness.' The event served as a platform for nearly 20 students from classes IX to XII to share innovative ideas on holistic wellness. The discussion emphasized that wellness is multidimensional, covering physical fitness, yoga, emotional stability, and intellectual growth. A highlight of the session was the focus on the revival of traditional alternative medicines and the critical importance of social interaction in maintaining a healthy lifestyle. The speakers advocated for an integrated approach where mental health is given equal priority to physical health. The event was highly insightful, encouraging students to take charge of their well-being in a holistic manner. It was a successful initiative that empowered students to contribute meaningfully to the wellness discourse.

(iii) The tigers in the panel that she made Will go on prancing, proud and unafraid. What is the tone of the poet reflected in the above lines? (Aunt Jennifer's Tigers)
(iv) What is Pablo Neruda's complaint against fishermen ? (Keeping Quiet)
(v) How and why does Keats relate 'mighty dead' to the 'Thing of Beauty'? (A Thing of Beauty)
(vi) 'Jansie, knowing they were both earmarked for the biscuit factory, became melancholy'. What inference about Jansie's character is drawn from the above line? (Going Places)

sub_questions.text_english: Inference about German imposition
sub_questions.solution: This rhetorical question expresses Franz's indignation at the imposition of the German language. It implies that while people can be forced to change their language, nature itself—symbolized by the pigeons cooing in their natural way—cannot be subjugated or forced to adopt human cultural dominance.

sub_questions.text_english: Father's reaction
sub_questions.solution: This statement highlights the father's lack of sensitivity toward the child's genuine fear. While the father views the ocean waves as a source of fun, his laughter reveals he is dismissive of his son's traumatic experience, failing to recognize the depth of terror the boy felt.

sub_questions.text_english: Tone of the poet

key_points: Contrast between Aunt and her creation.

sub_questions.solution: The poet's tone is one of admiration and reverence for the tigers' spirit. She contrasts their 'proud and unafraid' nature with Aunt Jennifer's own suppressed and terrified life, suggesting a desire for the liberation and strength that the aunt created through her art.

sub_questions.text_english: Neruda's complaint
sub_questions.solution: Neruda complains that fishermen are engaged in the thoughtless destruction of marine life. He believes that humanity is so obsessed with its own activities and progress that it fails to realize the pain and ecological damage inflicted upon other living creatures for personal gain.

sub_questions.text_english: Keats and mighty dead
sub_questions.solution: Keats relates the 'mighty dead' to a 'thing of beauty' because their noble deeds, sacrifices, and stories serve as an eternal inspiration. Their legacy remains alive in our memories, offering hope and comfort, which acts as a permanent, beautiful influence that counteracts life's sorrows.

sub_questions.text_english: Jansie's character
sub_questions.solution: This line depicts Jansie as a pragmatist who is fully aware of her social and economic reality. Unlike Sophie, she does not harbor unrealistic dreams; instead, she accepts her predetermined fate of working in the biscuit factory with a sense of melancholic realism.

sub_questions.text_english: Charley's fascination
sub_questions.solution: Charley was fascinated with Galesburg because it represented a simpler, more peaceful era, characterized by idyllic summers, expansive lawns, and friendly community life. It served as a refuge for him, offering an escape from the anxiety, stress, and insecurity of modern, twentieth-century life.

sub_questions.text_english: Dr. Sadao as a husband
sub_questions.solution: Dr. Sadao is a protective and considerate husband who deeply values his wife Hana's peace of mind. While he remains committed to his professional duty as a doctor, he realizes that the presence of the American prisoner is causing Hana distress and chooses to act to restore her comfort.

sub_questions.text_english: Annan and Bama bond
sub_questions.solution: The bond between Annan and Bama is that of an insightful mentor and a receptive student. Annan acts as a guide, providing Bama with the social and political consciousness necessary to understand the reality of caste discrimination. Bama respects Annan’s wisdom, and he trusts her with the truth.

(b) Compare the joy that both Edla and Saheb experience after receiving their respective gifts. (The Rattrap, Lost Spring)

sub_questions.text_english: Speech on Nature
sub_questions.solution: Good morning to one and all! After reading both the poems, I strongly believe that preserving nature is not an option, but a necessity for human survival. In 'Keeping Quiet', Pablo Neruda teaches us the power of stillness and introspection. If we pause our destructive activities, the earth can heal, and we may finally recognize our shared humanity. Similarly, Keats in 'A Thing of Beauty' asserts that nature is an eternal source of joy, providing a 'bower quiet' that alleviates life's suffering. As members of the Eco Club, we must advocate for a lifestyle that respects the earth’s rhythm. Nature provides us with life, shelter, and beauty; if we continue to prioritize exploitation, we will lose this sanctuary forever. Let us pledge to protect our environment, for in preserving the natural world, we are truly preserving ourselves. Thank you.

sub_questions.text_english: Comparison of joy

key_points: Comparison of joy based on context

sub_questions.solution: The joy experienced by Edla and Saheb, while disparate in context, reflects the transformative power of compassion and necessity. For Edla, joy stems from the act of giving; she offers the peddler kindness and trust, believing in his potential for goodness. Her gift is spiritual, an extension of her empathetic nature. In contrast, Saheb, a ragpicker living in extreme poverty, finds joy in material things that most take for granted, such as a pair of discarded shoes. His joy is one of survival and relief from the harsh conditions of his life. While Edla’s joy is a conscious choice of generosity, Saheb’s joy is the simple fulfillment of a basic need. Ultimately, both instances highlight how gestures of kindness, whether material or emotional, can illuminate the lives of those marginalized by society, bringing a brief moment of happiness in challenging times.

questions.text_english:
Answer ANY ONE of the following two questions, in 120-150 words:
(a) Imagine you are Derry speaking at the funeral of Mr. Lamb highlighting Mr. Lamb's optimism and the change he brought about in your attitude towards life. (On the Face of it)
(b) After having escaped from Japan with the help of Dr. Sadao, Tom (the prisoner of war) writes an article highlighting how Sadao's actions demonstrated the importance of humanity and living in harmony. (The Enemy)

sub_questions.text_english: Derry's speech
sub_questions.solution:
Dear friends,
I will be eternally grateful to Mr. Lamb. When I first met him, I was a cynical, bitter boy who hated the world because of my burnt face. I hid from people and rejected kindness, thinking everyone was judgmental. But Mr. Lamb was different; he had his own scars, yet his heart was full of light. He taught me that life isn't about what you lose, but about what you choose to see. He made me realize that I had a life worth living, and my face didn't define me. His garden became my sanctuary where I learned to laugh and be myself. Without his relentless optimism and wisdom, I would still be hiding in the shadows. He taught me to step out and face the world, not as a victim, but as a person capable of love. I have lost a mentor, but I have found myself because of him.

sub_questions.text_english: Tom's article
sub_questions.solution:
HUMANITY BEYOND BORDERS: A TESTAMENT TO HARMONY
By Tom

War often blinds us to our shared existence, turning enemies into mere targets. However, my experience in Japan, specifically at the hands of Dr. Sadao, was a lesson in the transcendent power of humanity. Despite being a prisoner of war, I was not treated as an object of hatred, but as a life in need. Dr. Sadao was torn between his duty to his country and his oath as a physician, yet he chose to honor his Hippocratic oath above all else. His actions demonstrated that compassion is not conditional, nor should it be suppressed by national enmity. By ensuring my safety and freedom, he showcased that living in harmony requires the courage to act with humanity even in the most hostile times. True peace is found when we see the person beneath the uniform, proving that the bond of humanity is stronger than any war.
